target_customer: Expecting and new parents looking for local parent communities, free to use
problem: New parents struggled to meet other local parents, and advice lived in fragmented mailing lists, Google Groups and private Facebook groups. Parenthoods offered one mobile network per locality.
business_model: Free consumer social network, no revenue model stated at launch

founders.name: Siobhan Quinn
founders.background_notes: YC page: first product manager at Foursquare and an early software engineer at Google; later Director at YouTube leading community products.

founders.name: Jeni Axline
education: University of Washington (TechCrunch says the founders met there)
founders.background_notes: Director of Production at Say Media per TechCrunch; the idea came from her own experience becoming a mother.

competitors.name: Golden Gate Mothers Group
competitors.what: Paid local parent group with annual and joining fees

competitors.name: BabyCenter, CafeMom, TheBump, Circle of Moms
Facebook private groups and Meetup
competitors.what: Local mom groups on general platforms

technical_complexity.rationale: A location-based social app with groups and messaging, standard consumer mobile engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Local network effects would help if density was reached, but Facebook groups and Meetup offered free substitutes.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch named Google, Yahoo and Facebook as the main threats. The app later ended up under Wonderschool, a child care platform, with deal terms not public.

market_need_then: About a quarter of early users were active daily at launch in August 2014 with a few hundred testers, and parents were already organizing in mailing lists and Facebook groups.

branding.domain_note: Used parenthoods.co at YC time per the dataset URL.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned as made exclusively for parents, by parents.

branding.brand_signature: Only YC S14 company with two female cofounders, widely noted in launch coverage

rebrands.why: Became a Wonderschool product after the company was acquired; date not found.

brand_strength.rationale: Launch coverage by TechCrunch and VentureBeat gave awareness, but there is no evidence of merch, mascot or word of mouth beyond that.

outcome_analysis: Parenthoods launched a local parenting network in August 2014 and raised a 1.32 million dollar seed in November 2014 from Slow Ventures, Lowercase and others. It competed with free incumbents such as Facebook groups and BabyCenter. YC lists it as acquired and it now lives on as Parenthoods by Wonderschool, but no source stated the date, buyer or terms, so the exit is likely a small asset deal. The failure factor is a judgment from the lack of later funding news, not a stated cause.
notes: Website parenthoods.co was not fetched separately; the Wonderschool blog and App Store listing show the product under Wonderschool as of 2023. The seed was confirmed by VentureBeat (opened) and a TechCrunch headline snippet of 1.32 million dollars. No source states that Wonderschool acquired the company; the exit acquirer is left null. Stage label seed is stated by the source.
